name: AWS Nitro System
description: Hardware + software stack underpinning all modern EC2 instances. Components: Nitro Cards (offload network/storage I/O), local NVMe storage, Nitro Security Chip (motherboard-integrated, boot-firmware integrity), Nitro Hypervisor (lightweight KVM-derived hypervisor — only used on virtualized instance types). Bare-metal instance types skip the hypervisor while keeping all other Nitro components.

name: Nitro Hypervisor
description: Lightweight hypervisor managing memory + CPU allocation on virtualized Nitro EC2 instances. AWS-internal; not user-accessible. Indistinguishable-from-bare-metal performance for most workloads. KVM-derived. Cross-domain link: AWS Fargate Linux tasks run in Firecracker microVMs that are SEPARATE from the Nitro Hypervisor — Firecracker is the inner-VMM, Nitro is the outer-VMM (when not bare-metal).

name: Bare-Metal EC2 instance
description: .metal-suffix instance types (i3.metal, m5.metal, m5d.metal, r5.metal, z1d.metal, c5.metal, m6i.metal, m7i.metal, etc.). EC2 instance types that expose the underlying hardware directly — no Nitro Hypervisor between guest and CPU. Boot is slower (up to 20 minutes initial verification of all hardware/firmware). Use cases: workloads requiring Intel VT (nested KVM, Firecracker host); license-bound software needing non-virtualized environment (Oracle, ESXi); custom hypervisors.

name: Nitro Security Chip
description: Motherboard-integrated chip that monitors firmware + hardware on every Nitro instance, including bare-metal. Continuously verifies that firmware hasn't been tampered with. Foundation of AWS's hardware-supply-chain integrity claim.

name: Nitro Card
description: PCIe cards that offload network/storage I/O from the host CPU. Net Nitro Card handles ENA (Elastic Network Adapter) + EFA (Elastic Fabric Adapter); Storage Nitro Card handles EBS + local NVMe.

name: Nitro version matrix (v2-v6)
description: Cumulative feature stack. v2: ENA enhanced networking + Traffic Mirroring. v3: 100 Gbps/card + encryption-in-transit. v4: 100/170 Gbps/card + ENA Express + RDMA read/write on select types. v5: 200 Gbps/card. v6: 400 Gbps/card + reduced default TCP idle timeout (432000s → 350s). New networking features added cumulatively.

name: Bare-metal boot time (~20 min)
description: Bare-metal launches go through full hardware/firmware verification — instance can take 20+ min from 'running' state to network-reachable. Plan AMI rotations + auto-scaling around this. Subsequent boots from cache may be faster.

name: Nested KVM (Firecracker host)
description: Bare-metal instances expose Intel VT-x / AMD-V to the guest, enabling nested virtualization. Critical for running KVM-based workloads (e.g., Firecracker as the inner-VMM). The C8i/M8i/R8i Nitro v6 instances ALSO support nested-virt without being bare-metal — but pay ~10% CPU overhead. Pure bare-metal has no nested-virt tax.

name: Bare-metal use case: licensing
description: Some commercial software (Oracle, Microsoft) prohibits or extra-charges for virtualized environments. Bare-metal EC2 lets enterprises run such software on AWS without licensing penalty.

name: Bare-metal use case: hardware-perf-sensitive
description: Workloads that need direct access to CPU performance counters (perf, PMU events), undisturbed cache + TLB, or specialized hardware features (Intel VT for nested-virt, SGX). Examples: HFT systems, perf-research, HPC, latency-sensitive databases.
